short: Positive entropy for the standard map

title.title: Positive metric entropy for the standard map
title.subtitle: Claim: past some $k_0$, every Chirikov standard map has positive metric entropy for area

beats.text: $f_k(x,y) = (x + y + k\sin 2\pi x,\ y + k\sin 2\pi x)$ loses expansion where $\cos 2\pi x = 0$
Sinai asked for a positive-measure set of $k$. The claim covers every $k \ge k_0$
Elliptic islands kept blocking proofs for decades

plain: Kick a spinning rotor harder and harder: is its chaos real on a sizable region, or confined to thin cracks?

steps: Pesin's formula turns entropy into a rate of stretching
So show nearby points pull apart on a region of positive area
Control the stretching lost near the lines where it stalls

boxes: control losses near the critical lines

voice.text: Kick a rotor harder and harder. Pictures show a chaotic sea, but islands kept blocking proofs.
Entropy equals the stretching rate, so prove stretching on a sizable region.
Claimed: positive entropy for every large kick.
